steps_raw.instruction: Isolation of Nuclei from Adult Mouse Brain Tissue
Scope and Applicability: Isolation of nuclei from microdissected mouse brain tissue sections for FPCR and/or RNA-seq analysis.
Acute adult mouse brain tissue slices (200-500 µm thick)
RNase Away RNase Decontamination Solution (VWR 17810-491)
Nuclease free water (Life Technologies AM9932)
10X PBS, pH 7.4 (Ambion/Life Technologies AM9625)
Sucrose (VWR 97061 or equivalent, Ultra Pure RNase DNase free sucrose)
2 M Potassium Chloride, RNase free (KCl; Ambion/Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9640G)
1 M Magnesium Chloride, RNase free (MgCl2; Ambion/Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9530G)
1 M Tris Buffer, pH 8.0 (Ambion/Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9856)
RNasin Plus RNase Inhibitor (Promega N2615)
Triton X-100 (Molecular biology grade, Sigma T8787)
100 mM DL Dithiothreitol, molecular biology grade (DTT; Promega P1171 or equivalent)
BSA; Ultrapure, RNase-free (OmniPur EMD Chemicals 2905)
Protease Inhibitor Cocktail, 50X (Promega G6521)
Molecular Biology Grade Ethanol (Sigma E7023 or equivalent)
(optional) Trypan Blue, 0.4% (Gibco/Thermo Fisher Scientific 15250-061)
DAPI (Thermo Fisher Scientific D1306)
Millimark mouse anti-NeuN monoclonal antibody clone A60, PE conjugated (EMD Millipore FCMAB317PE)
anti-SATB2 rabbit monoclonal antibody, Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated (Abcam EPNCIR130A)
PE mouse IgG1k isotype control (BD Biosciences, 550617)
Alexa Fluor 647 mouse IgG1k isotype control (BD Biosciences, 557783)
15 ml conical tubes (VWR 21008-670 or equivalent)
50 ml conical tubes (VWR 21008-951 or equivalent)
1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes, PCR grade RNase-free (Eppendorf, DNA LoBind, 0030108051)
5 ml Polystyrene round bottom tubes with filter (BD Falcon 352235)
30 µm cell strainer (MACS SmartStrainers, Miltenyi Biotech 130-098-458)
Bottle-top vacuum filter system; 0.22 µm pore size, 250 ml (EMD Millipore SCGPU02RE, Millipore Steritop or equivalent) or 0.45 µm (Corning 430516 purchased as VWR 28199-814, 28199-818 or equivalent)
Syringe filter, 0.22 µm (EMD Millipore, Millex PES 30 mm sterile syringe filters, SLGP033RB or equivalent)
30 ml syringe, luer lock (Becton Dickinson BD309650)
Sylgard-coated dishes
Fluorescent dissecting microscope, camera and image acquisition software (Nikon SMZ1500, or equivalent)
Disposable Plastic Handle Microknives, 15 and/or 22.5 degree blade (Fine Science Tools 10318-12 or equivalent)
Razor blade (VWR 94-0391 or equivalent)
2 ml Serological pipettes
5 ml Serological pipettes
10 ml Serological pipettes
200 proof Ethyl Alcohol (Greenfield Global E200G)

Tube rotator (Miltenyi MACS Mini or equivalent)
Phase contrast inverted microscope

Isolated nuclei from mouse brain tissue for transcriptomic profiling.

Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor
This protocol is extremely sensitive to RNase contamination; ensure that you have been properly trained using sterile techniques before starting this protocol.
Prepare stock solutions as needed
20 ml 10% BSA (made with Nuclease-free Water)
Weigh out and add 2 g Ultrapure, RNase-free BSA (final concentration 10%) to a 50 ml conical tube.
Using a serological pipette, measure 20 ml of Nuclease-free water and dispense into the 50 ml conical tube containing BSA.
Vortex the solution until BSA powder is fully dissolved in the solution.
Allow solution to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes to reduce foaming.
Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into a clean 50ml conical tube. Label the tube with the date and name of the solution.
Store the 10% BSA in nuclease-free water at 4°C for up to two weeks.
20 ml 10% Triton X-100 in Nuclease-free Water
Using a serological pipette, measure 18 ml of Nuclease-free water into a 50 ml conical tube.
Add 2 ml of Triton X-100 to the 18 ml of water.
Mix thoroughly by vortexing until Triton-X 100 is fully dissolved.
Allow the solution to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes to reduce foaming.
Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into a clean 50 ml conical tube. Label the tube with the date and name of the solution.
Store the 10% Triton-X 100 in nuclease-free water at 4°C for up to 30 days.
250 ml Nuclei Isolation Media (NIM) pH 8.0
Measure 200 ml of Nuclease-free water and dispense it into an RNase free 250 ml bottle.
Using a serological pipette, measure and add 2.5 ml 1 M Tris Buffer, pH 8.0 (final concentration 10 mM).
Weigh out and add 21.45 g Sucrose (final concentration 250 mM).
Using a serological pipette, measure and dispense 3.13 ml of 2 M KCl (final concentration 25 mM).
Using a serological pipette, measure and dispense 1.25 ml of 1 M MgCl2 (final concentration 5 mM).
Place the cap on the bottle and shake the solution until the sucrose is fully dissolved.
Using a serological pipette, adjust final volume to 250 ml with Nuclease-free water.
Filter the solution using a 0.22 µm (Millipore Steritop) or 0.45 µm (Corning) filter system
Using Tygon tubing, attach the filter system to a 1000 ml filter flask, and then attach the filter flask to a house vacuum line or vacuum pump.
Turn on the vacuum line or pump.
Store the Nuclei Isolation Media at 4°C for up to two weeks.
50X Protease Inhibitor Cocktail
Remove the 50X Protease Inhibitor Cocktail from the -20°C freezer and use a P1000 pipette to immediately add 1 ml of molecular biology grade 100% Ethanol.
Pipette up and down 5-10 times with a P1000 pipette to dissolve the Protease Inhibitor Cocktail.
Transfer the solution to a PCR grade 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube (Eppendorf).
Store the solution at 4°C for up to 30 days.
10 ml DAPI in Nuclease-free Water
Dissolve 10 mg of DAPI in 10 ml of Nuclease free water to produce a 1 mg/ml stock solution.
Divide the solution into 1 ml aliquots in labeled 1.5 ml RNase free microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf, DNA LoBind).
Freeze the aliquots at -20ºC for up to six months.

At the time of use, remove an aliquot of DAPI from the -20ºC freezer and thaw. Dilute the 1 mg/ml DAPI stock 1:10 in nuclease-free water (i.e. add 100 µl of 1 mg/ml DAPI to 900 µl of nuclease-free water) to a final concentration of 0.1 mg/ml.
Store 0.1 mg/ml DAPI at 4°C for up to 1 month. The 1 mg/ml stock can be stored at 4°C for up to 3 months or returned to the -20°C freezer.
Prepare fresh solutions as needed
10 ml Blocking Buffer
Using a serological pipette, measure and dispense 8.2 ml of Nuclease-free water into a 15 ml conical tube.
Using a P1000 pipette, measure and add 1 ml of 10X PBS, pH 7.4
Using a P1000 pipette, measure and add 0.8 ml (800 µl) of 10% BSA in nuclease-free water (final concentration 0.8%).
Vortex the solution briefly to mix.
Using a P200 pipette, measure and add 50 µl of 40 U/µl RNasin Plus RNAse inhibitor (final concentration 0.5%, 0.2 U/µl)
Invert the solution 5-10 times to mix (do not vortex after addition of RNase inhibitor).
The blocking buffer must be made fresh on the day it is to be used.
Store on ice or at 4°C until ready to use.
25 ml Homogenization Buffer
Using a serological pipette, measure and dispense 24.125 ml of Nuclei Isolation Media (NIM) pH 8.0 into a 50 ml conical tube.
Using a P20 pipette, measure and dispense 25 µl of 100 mM DTT stock (final concentration 0.1 mM).
Using a P1000 pipette, measure and add 500 µl 50X Protease inhibitor cocktail (final concentration 1X).
Using a P200 pipette, measure and add 125 µl 40 U/µl RNAsin Plus (final concentration 0.5%, 0.2 U/µl).
Using a P200 pipette, measure and add 250 µl 10% Triton X-100 in Nuclease-free Water (final concentration 0.1%).
Mix the solution by inverting the tube 5-10 times. Do not vortex after the addition of the RNasin Plus RNase inhibitor.
The homogenization buffer must be made fresh on the day it is to be used.
Store on ice or at 4ºC until ready to use.
Methodology/Procedures:
Preparation of tissue samples
Spray down all work surfaces with RNase Away
Prepare the homogenization buffer by mixing NIM as described above and place the solution on ice or in a 4°C fridge.

Dounce homogenizers should be soaked in RNAse Away solution overnight prior to use. After soaking in RNase away, rinse the dounces very well in MilliQ water. Ensure that all RNase Away solution is removed from the homogenizers. After rinsing in MilliQ water, use nuclease-free water for one final thorough rinse of the dounces. Place the dounces on a clean kimwipe to dry. Once the dounces are dry, wrap the body of the dounce and the pestles in a clean kimwipe, place them in a clean secondary container (RNase free pipette tip box or Ziploc bag), and transfer them to a 4°C fridge to cool. Dounces should be cooled for at least 30 minutes prior to use.
Reference AF0100 Slice Preparation with Tissue Dissociation -Mouse SOP to generate acute slices containing ROI.
Using a P1000 pipette, cover the bottom of a Sylgard-coated dissecting dish with ACSF.I (RP0218).
Place first tissue slice containing ROI in the Sylgard-coated dish and transfer to a fluorescent dissecting microscope with an attached camera.
Dissect out regions of interest.
Acquire brightfield overview image of whole slice.
Using microdissecting tools, dissect the regions of interest, leaving them in the cutout section.
Acquire brightfield overview image of the slice with ROI cutouts.
Acquire brightfield zoomed-in image of the ROI cutouts.
Using the microdissecting tools, separate the ROI cutouts from the rest of the tissue.
Attach a tip to a P1000 pipette. Using a razor blade, cut off the end of the pipette tip to create a larger opening.

Using this enlarged tip, aspirate the ROI cutouts, along with a small amount (~30 µl) of the ACSF that is in the dish and dispense into a 1.5 ml Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube labeled with sample information.
Repeat steps 8.1.6 – 8.1.8.1 for the desired number of slices.
Combine several pieces of dry ice with approximately ~200 ml of 200 proof Ethyl alcohol in a small ice bucket to create a slurry.
Using a P1000 pipette, aspirate as much ACSF.I as possible from samples, leaving only tissue pieces in tube.
Hold each sample tube in slurry for 30-60 seconds (or until visibly frozen) and keep on dry ice until ready to continue protocol.

Remove the dounce homogenizer(s) from the fridge and place the body of the dounce into an ice bucket containing wet ice (do not allow ice to enter the top of the dounce). Keep the pestles wrapped in the clean kimwipe until ready to use.
Note: number of dounces required will equal the number of samples to process.
If dissected samples were frozen, add 1 ml homogenization buffer to each sample tube and place on wet ice to thaw.

If proceeding directly from microdissection without freezing, remove as much ACSF.I as possible from samples, leaving only tissue pieces in tube. Add 1 ml homogenization buffer to each sample and keep on wet ice.

For each sample, transfer tissue and all homogenization buffer to a dounce. Place the loose pestle (note – pestles come pre-labeled “loose” and “tight”) into the dounce and homogenize the tissue with 10 strokes of the pestle. Keep the pestle submerged in the solution while douncing to avoid forming bubbles. Keep the body of the dounce in wet ice while homogenizing to avoid heating sample. Note: for large chunks of tissue, additional homogenization may be required. However, when douncing large pieces of tissue, the presence of some large (>1 mm) pieces of white matter is normal and increasing the number of dounce strokes will not effectively remove these pieces.

Remove the loose pestle and place the tight pestle into the dounce. Note: When removing pestles, carefully examine the sides of the pestle and dounce body for any tissue pieces that may be stuck on the glass. Rinse any of these pieces back into the dounce body with a small amount (~200 µl or less) of homogenization buffer.
Homogenize the tissue with ~10 strokes of the tight pestle. Keep the pestle submerged in the solution while douncing to avoid forming bubbles. Keep the dounce on ice during the homogenization.

Add an additional 2 ml of homogenization buffer to the dounce. Using a P1000 pipet tip transfer the homogenate out of the dounce and pass it through a 30 µm cell strainer into a 15 ml conical tube to remove large debris. The final volume of homogenization buffer is 3 ml per sample.
Multiple strainers may be required to avoid clogging depending on the amount of tissue in sample.
Spin the homogenate in a 4°C centrifuge for 10 min, 900 x g, to pellet the nuclei.

After centrifugation, a visible pellet should be apparent on the bottom of the tube. However, when working with small pieces of microdissected tissue the pellet may be difficult to visualize. Note: when working with large tissue chunks the supernatant may still be cloudy after centrifugation.
Remove the supernatant leaving approximately 50 µl of solution sitting above the pellet at the bottom of the tube.

To the pelleted nuclei add 500 µl of blocking buffer, resuspend by pipetting up and down gently 5 times, and incubate on ice for up to 15 minutes. Transfer resuspended nuclei preparations to a 1.5 ml RNase-free microcentrifuge tube (Eppendorf DNA LoBind).

Optional: From each sample, remove 10 µl of the nuclei resuspension and add it to 10 µl of 0.4% Trypan Blue. Mix by pipetting up and down 5 times, incubate for 1 minute at RT, and then pipette 10 µl of solution into a disposable hemocytometer. Examine nuclei on inverted phase-contrast microscope and assess the quality of the nuclei preparations. Note the presence and frequency of damaged nuclei (i.e. nuclei lacking a clear, uniform border) and, if desired, quantify yield of nuclei (number per ml).

Prepare control tubes: Two controls are run with each experiment, a DAPI labeled control and an isotype control. Create the control tubes by removing a small amount of sample from one or more of the resuspended nuclei preparations. For example, if working with microdissected cortical layers, remove 50 µl of nuclei resuspension from the layers with the highest nuclei yield to a clean 1.5 ml tube. Add 450 µl of blocking buffer to each control tube to bring the final volumes to 500 µl.
The same sample should not be used for both controls to ensure sufficient volume for desired collections.
Record which sample you use for each control
Set the DAPI only sample aside on ice.
To the Isotype control sample, add PE conjugated IgG1k at a final dilution of 1:250.
If using Satb2 (or other antibody conjugated to AF647) add AF647 conjugated IgG1k isotype antibody also at final dilution of 1:250.
For example: for samples suspended in 500 µl of blocking buffer, add 2 µl of each IgG1k isotype control for 1:250 dilution.
To the remaining samples to be stained with NeuN antibody, add Millimark mouse anti-NeuN PE conjugated antibody at a final dilution of 1:500.
If also staining with other antibodies in addition to NeuN, add them to each sample at the appropriate dilution:
If combining NeuN and Satb2 antibodies, add Abcam anti-SATB2 AF647 conjugated antibody also at a final dilution of 1:500.
E.g., for samples suspended in 500 µl of blocking buffer, add 1 µl of antibody for 1:500 dilution.
Incubate all the tubes (including the controls) on a tube rotator in a 4°C refrigerator for 30 minutes.

Following antibody incubation, spin all samples in a refrigerated centrifuge (4°C), 400 x g, 5 minutes. A visible pellet of nuclei should be present on the bottom of the tube unless working with very small microdissected tissue samples. Use a swinging bucket rotor to spin tubes so that the pellet falls to the bottom of the tube rather than the side of the tube. This will prevent pellet loss during removal of supernatant. 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes can be balanced in a 15 ml conical tube rotor or a 5 ml Polystyrene round-bottom tube rotor for this purpose.
Remove the supernatant leaving ~50 µl of buffer above the pellets and pipette in 500 µl of clean blocking buffer. Resuspend the pellets by gently pipetting up and down 5 times.
To each tube, add DAPI at a final concentration of 0.1 µg/ml (dilute from 0.1 mg/ml stock) and mix by gently tapping each tube.
Prior to FACS, filter each sample through the cap of a 5 ml Polystyrene round bottom FACS tube.
Keep tubes on ice or at 4°C and proceed to FACS.
Dispose of any unused blocking buffer down the sink.
Dispose of any unused homogenization buffer down the sink.
Disposal of Tissue and Contaminated Material:
All tissue and contaminated material must be disposed of via the Biohazardous Waste stream in an approved Biohazard Waste Container.

Clean the dounce homogenizers with copious amounts of tap water. Transfer the dounces to a clean container filled with RNase Away solution and allow them to soak overnight. The next day, rinse the dounces with copious amounts of MilliQ water and, finally, rinse well with nuclease free water. Thoroughly dry the dounce homogenizers with clean kimwipes and wrap each dounce and associated pestles in a clean kimwipe. Store the dounces wrapped in kimwipes in a clean RNase-free pipet tip box or Ziploc bag at room temperature until next use.
